transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because things have gotten rough since they made me the acting workflow lead at the warehouse. I walk in already tense, and I’ve been snapping over little SAP errors—stuff I used to handle better. I’m also missing cycle-count deadlines I never used to miss. By the time I get home, I’m just drained… I don’t even feel up to playing basketball or working on my sketches.
Are you still enjoying basketball and sketching when you do find the time and energy for them?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t done either much lately, so it’s hard to say. When I think about them, they still seem like things I like, but I just haven’t had it in me to really get into them.
Do you feel like you're getting any pleasure from the things you're still managing to do?
I don’t really know. I mean, I get through stuff, but I haven’t stopped to notice if I’m actually enjoying any of it. It’s more like I’m just doing what needs to get done.
Have you been feeling guilty or worthless about anything lately?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get frustrated with myself when I mess something up or fall behind, but I wouldn’t say I feel worthless or guilty in a big way. It’s more just… annoyed at myself, I guess.
Have you been feeling anxious about anything lately?

Yeah. Mostly about work. Since they made me the acting workflow lead, I feel tense before I even walk into the warehouse. Little things, like SAP errors, set me off more than they should, and I’ve been missing cycle-count deadlines I used to handle fine. Then by the time I get home, I’m just wiped out.
Have you been feeling sad most of the time lately?
I don’t think I’d say sad most of the time. More stressed and worn down than sad. I have off moments where I feel down, but it doesn’t feel like that’s the main thing.
Do you feel anxious even when you're not at work or thinking about work?

Not really. It mostly seems tied to work. Like, ever since they put me in that acting workflow lead spot, I’m tense before I even get into the warehouse. Then stuff like SAP errors gets under my skin, and I’m missing cycle-count deadlines I used to make. By the time I’m home, I’m mostly just drained—too wiped out to play basketball or work on my sketches.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?
Not really, no. I haven’t noticed my weight changing much lately.
Do you ever feel anxious when you're not thinking about work or anything related to the warehouse?

Not really. It’s pretty much connected to the warehouse and that acting lead role. If I’m not thinking about work, I don’t usually feel anxious—I’m more just drained when I get home, and I haven’t had the energy for basketball or my sketches.
Do you ever wake up in the morning feeling anxious for no particular reason?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can wake up uneasy if I know I’m heading into work, but not really for no reason that I’ve noticed.
Do you feel anxious when you're doing things you normally enjoy, like playing basketball or working on sketches?

I don’t really get anxious while doing those things, because honestly I’m barely doing them anymore. I stopped showing up for basketball, and I haven’t been keeping up with my sketching time. Work’s been taking over so much that even my supervisor brought up missed cycle-count deadlines during a performance check-in.
Is there anything outside of work that you've been worrying about lately?

Not really, no. It’s mostly the work situation. Since they put me in that acting workflow lead role, I feel tense before I even get into the warehouse, and then I’m snapping over small SAP mistakes or missing cycle-count deadlines I used to stay on top of. By the time I get home, I’m just too drained to play basketball or work on my sketches.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been tracking it closely. Some nights I feel like I’m not rested, but I couldn’t say I’ve noticed a clear sleep problem.
Are you avoiding certain tasks or situations at work because they make you feel anxious?

I’m not sure I’d call it avoiding. I don’t think I’m skipping specific tasks on purpose because I’m anxious. I just know some parts of the day feel harder to face, but I haven’t really noticed a clear pattern like that.
Are you finding it hard to concentrate or make decisions when you're not at work?
I don’t think so, not in a clear way. When I’m off work, I might be tired or kind of distracted, but I haven’t really noticed trouble making decisions or concentrating outside of work.
Do you feel like you're anxious almost all the time, even when there's no obvious reason to be?

I don’t think it’s all the time, no. I do feel anxious here and there, but I can usually connect it to something. I haven’t noticed feeling anxious for no reason most of the day or anything like that.
Is your anxiety mostly about the responsibilities of being the acting workflow lead or more about being at the warehouse in general?

Mostly the acting lead responsibilities, I think. I wasn’t like this just being in the warehouse before. Since they put me in that role, I come in already tense, and little things like SAP errors set me off. I’ve been missing cycle-count deadlines I used to stay on top of, and by the time I get home I’m just wiped out.
Do you feel like your anxiety about work is affecting your relationships with family or friends?

Yeah, I think it is. I’ve stopped showing up for basketball, and I’m not really taking my usual time to sketch either. It’s like work is taking over more of my life than it should. Even my supervisor had to bring up the missed cycle-count deadlines in a performance check-in, so it’s spilling over in a few ways.
Are you finding that your overall daily life, outside of work, is being significantly impacted by how you've been feeling lately?

Yeah, it is. It’s not just staying at work anymore. My supervisor already had to talk to me about missed cycle-count deadlines, and outside of work I’ve stopped going to basketball and I’m not making time to sketch like I usually do. It feels like work is kind of taking over everything.
Are there other parts of your daily life, beyond work and activities like basketball and sketching, that you feel are being affected by how you've been feeling lately?

Mostly it’s those same areas, honestly. Work problems are following me home, and it’s gotten to the point where my supervisor had to bring up the missed cycle-count deadlines. Outside of that, I’ve stopped showing up for basketball and I’m not taking my normal time to sketch. It just feels like work is taking over more of my life than it should.
